is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae, Anopheles arabiensis, and Anopheles funestus (p. 3, 5, 7).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Tested for Vgsc-1014F and Vgsc-1014S (Vgsc L995F and L995S) using TaqMan assay (p. 5, p. 9).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 9 states: 'The Vgsc gene mutation was found in all tested A gambiae with co-occurrence of Vgsc-1014F and Vgsc-1014S in 22 (9%) of 234 A gambiae mosquitoes. No mutation was found in the 247 A arabiensis tested.'

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected using CDC light traps from March 2015 to December 2016 across 48 clusters in Muleba district, Kagera region, Tanzania (p. 3, 5).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary cluster randomised controlled trial evaluating PBO LLINs and IRS (p. 1, 3).

sub_country_location.evidence: Muleba district, Kagera region, northwest Tanzania (40 villages / 48 clusters) (p. 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito surveillance was conducted from March 2015 to December 2016 (p. 5).

duplicate_risk.evidence: New primary data collection within a specific RCT in Muleba district, Tanzania (March 2015 to December 2016).

supplement.evidence: The appendix is only referenced for epidemiological per-protocol analyses and net use data; no indication of missing supplementary genotype tables.

assessment.summary: This cluster randomised controlled trial in Muleba, Tanzania evaluated the effectiveness of PBO-LLINs and pirimiphos-methyl IRS. As part of entomological monitoring, 234 An. gambiae and 247 An. arabiensis were genotyped for Vgsc-1014F and Vgsc-1014S mutations, showing co-occurrence of 1014F and 1014S in 22 (9%) of An. gambiae and 0 mutations in An. arabiensis.
